name: Jianlibao (健力宝)
blurb: China's 1984 orange-honey sports soda, nicknamed "Oriental magic water"
title: What Is Jianlibao (健力宝)? China's 1984 Sports Drink
description: Jianlibao (健力宝) is a fizzy electrolyte sports drink created in Guangdong in 1984, drunk by China's Los Angeles Olympic team and dubbed "Oriental magic water".
answer: Jianlibao is a lightly carbonated, honey-sweetened electrolyte sports drink developed in 1984 at a liquor factory in Sanshui, Guangdong. Sold in cans, it went with China's team to the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics, where foreign press nicknamed it "Oriental magic water", and it became one of China's best-known drinks of the 1980s and 1990s. After several changes of ownership from 2002 it lost its lead, but it is still produced, including a retro 1984-style can.

body: Think of an orange-yellow, honeyed citrus soda with added electrolytes: a sports drink with bubbles. The early flavours were orange-honey and lemon-honey. Jianlibao says it was China's first drink with alkaline electrolytes and its first canned sports drink; the original was a 330 ml aluminium can decorated with a green running track and a discus thrower.

body: Jianlibao was at its height in the late 1980s and 1990s, when it was called China's top homegrown drink brand. After 2002, repeated ownership changes, a muddled move into trendy drinks and competition from Coca-Cola, Pepsi and newer brands turned it into a nostalgia brand. It never stopped production, and it is still sold in China, with the retro can aimed squarely at people who grew up with it.
